title: UniversallyConverging Representations of Matter Across Scientific Foundation Models
experiments_summary: The study analyzed 52 scientific foundation models spanning multiple input modalities (SMILES, SELFIES, 3D atomistic coordinates, protein sequences, protein structures, and natural language), architectures (equivariant and non-equivariant MLIPs, conservative vs. direct prediction models), and training domains (molecules, materials, proteins) across five datasets. Embeddings were extracted by passing ASE atom, graph, or SMILES string inputs into each model and saving the last hidden-layer features; node-level features were averaged across atoms to produce structure-level embeddings independent of input size. Five datasets were used: QM9 (134k small organic molecules, lowest-energy conformers used), sAlex (subsampled Alexandria inorganic materials dataset, in-distribution), OMat24 (118M inorganic materials structures, in-distribution), OMol25 (>100M molecule dataset, used as out-of-distribution benchmark), and RCSB Protein Data Bank (filtered to ~48,530 sequence-structure pairs). For each dataset, approximately 50,000 randomly sampled embeddings were selected for analysis (all 48,530 for RCSB), constrained by 192 GB CPU RAM. Three alignment metrics were computed pairwise across all model embedding sets for each dataset: (1) CKNNA (nearest-neighbor-restricted Centered Kernel Alignment), varying the neighborhood size k to test local sensitivity; (2) IDCor (Intrinsic Dimension Correlation), estimating mutual information between high-dimensional data manifolds; and (3) Information Imbalance, an asymmetric local metric quantifying directional information content between latent spaces. Intrinsic dimensionality was also computed per model per dataset. To analyze cross-modality alignment, pairwise CKNNA was computed between all model pairs on QM9 embeddings and results were averaged within architecture classes. To test convergence as a function of model performance, alignment of each model with the best-performing model was plotted against energy regression accuracy using OMat24 structures. In-distribution versus out-of-distribution alignment was compared by computing full CKNNA matrices on sAlex and OMat24 (in-distribution) versus OMol25 (out-of-distribution). For protein models, alignment between sequence-based models (e.g., ESM2) and structure-based models (e.g., ProteinMPNN) was computed using CKNNA on RCSB embeddings. An evolutionary tree of models was constructed using CKNNA-derived pairwise distances to visualize clustering by architecture, dataset, and modality. Information imbalance was additionally computed on OMol25 embeddings to probe directional representational differences between models on OOD data.
